sources: Luke 15:1-2 (tax collectors and sinners come near to hear him; Pharisees and scribes murmur, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them”)
Luke 15:3-4 (“Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?”)
Luke 15:5 (he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing)
Luke 15:6 (“Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!”)
Luke 15:7 (more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents)
Psalm 23:1 (“Yahweh is my shepherd”), in the teach step
Luke 15:11-32 (the lost son, the third story in the chapter; week one’s lesson)
Captions follow the World English Bible, lightly modernized

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever felt like the one who wandered off, from people, or from God?
options: then this story is about you. listen to who comes looking.
keep them in mind. this one is for them too.
good. you might be the one who goes looking someday.

steps.line: Tax collectors and outsiders crowded around Jesus. Some religious leaders grumbled, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
steps.label: Luke 15:1-2

steps.line: So Jesus told them a story. “Which of you, with a hundred sheep, if you lose one, doesn’t leave the ninety-nine and go after the lost one?”
steps.label: Luke 15:3-4

steps.q: How long do you guess the shepherd keeps looking?
o: Until sunset, then he gives up
steps.why: Until he finds it. No time limit.

steps.line: He goes out into the wild hills, and he keeps searching until he finds it.
steps.label: Luke 15:4

steps.pre: When he finds it, he doesn’t scold it. He lays it on his
steps.why: “Shoulders.” Not dragged or driven home. Carried, with joy.

steps.line: And when he finds it, he doesn’t scold it. He lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing, and carries it home.
steps.label: Luke 15:5

steps.line: He calls his friends and neighbors: “Rejoice with me!” Jesus said heaven rejoices like that over one lost person who turns back to God.
steps.label: Luke 15:6-7

steps.q: The shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep to find just one. Why does Jesus make the search sound so risky?
o: Because the ninety-nine were safe in a pen
To warn shepherds to count more often
To show how much one lost person is worth
steps.why: Luke says he leaves them “in the wilderness.” To the shepherd, the one is worth that risk.

steps.q: This is the first of three lost-and-found stories Jesus tells in a row. What are the other two?
o: A lost lamb and a lost servant
A lost coin and a lost son
A lost ring and a lost daughter
steps.why: Luke 15 tells all three: a sheep, a woman’s coin, and a son. Each one ends with a party.

say: here’s what i love. the shepherd doesn’t wait for the sheep to find its own way back. he goes.
christians see jesus as that shepherd, like the old psalm, “the lord is my shepherd.” and this is the first of three lost-and-found stories. you already know the third: the son who came home.

steps.q: The sheep doesn’t do anything to be found. It’s just carried home. What does that say about how God finds people?
o: God goes looking before we can make it back
God welcomes those who find their own way back
God forgives once we promise not to wander
steps.why: The sheep isn’t lectured or tested. It’s carried. That’s how the shepherd loves.

today.say: one is worth the walk. think of one person who’s drifted, from you, from friends, from church. reach out today: a message, a call, a knock. no lecture. just “i was thinking of you.”
options: then go after them today. gently.
then hear this: you’re being looked for. that’s the whole story.

tomorrow.title: The lost coin.
tomorrow.line: a woman turns her whole house upside down for one coin. then she throws a party.
